body: We stopped here on our way from Mirissa to Galle.It was fabulous.A great talk so informative.Baby turtles had hatched the night before.We saw all the injured turtles they care for.Many injured by boats…but what lovely Care they get here.It was a highlight of our 23 day trip round Sri Lanka.Definitely call in as takes less than an hour but you can stay longer.Cost 2000 Sri Lankan.Obviously you can then donate something to the running and upkeep…no pressure just a little box to donate if you wish.
title: Brilliant..so informative and such good work.

body: What they do for turtles is really exciting. They take them from the sea when they are injured, they care for them and help them get back to freedom, as well as protect their eggs from wild animals that try to destroy them...
title: Beautiful experience

body: Nothing fancy, but a must do if in the area. Great experience, good talk and most worthwhile. 2000rupiah per person. Xxx
title: Worth it

body: Very impressive talk about turtle conservation, rescue and rehabilitation to return to the wild. Well worth a visit to support this project.
title: Terrific Turtles

body: It's very cool to look at the turtles in their different stages of development. I think it’s a bit of a shame that the staff can’t speak enough English to talk to them about the animals (e.g. the reason why an adult turtle was in a tank).There are ONLY Green Turtles here, even if they look very different in some cases.A few years ago you could buy cucumber to feed it, that has unfortunately been discontinued...
title: Always happy

body: Sea Turtle Farm & Hatchery at Koggala (Sea turtle conservation project), is a not-for-profit organization which was started in 2010. They care for injured (mostly by fishing boats) and sick (mostly from eating plastic) turtles as well as hatchlings and have released more than 100,000 turtles back to the sea. Sri Lanka is home to five of the world's seven sea turtle species: Green turtles, Olive Ridley turtles, Hawksbill turtles, Loggerhead turtles, and Leatherback turtles.
title: Turtle Farm & Hatchery

body: We visited this amazing centre for Sea Turtle conservation, and the staff are knowledgeable, caring, and committed to the project.
title: Amazing Project

body: This was a turtle rescue and also semi hatchery. The man giving the talk was knowledgeable and seemed quite passionate. The turtles were in small enclosures which for the ones which were not going to be released seemed too small. Lovely chance for close up look at the turtles.
title: Turtle conservation

body: They are really doing some good here it seems and very responsible for the welfare of the turtles only releasing every night at sunset. you can buy tickets to be part of this which isn't on this site but worth knowing - its at 6pm most evenings in the season. Very friendly and knowledgable staff and as I say protecting the turtles ensuring they are treated well and not handled over much by visitors.
title: Outstanding turtle hatchery

body: After lots of research and working out our itinerary, we decided Sea Turtle Farm and Hatchery in Koggala was perfect. There are many such hatcheries and rescue projects across Sri Lanka, but not all seem to get universal positive reviews. This place is really special and the staff quite clearly care very deeply about these beautiful creatures. With a focus on rehabilitating injured or sick turtles (very sad boat accidents, fishing net traumas and plastic ingestion mainly), plus egg protection and collection – the work the staff do here on a very limited budget is remarkable. Your entrance fee goes directly to help this cause. It is fascinating to hear about the conservation work and turtles in general and we learnt a lot – all delivered in an accessible and friendly manner. On top of this, we were incredibly lucky and my family got to release x4 baby Olive Ridley turtles into the ocean (email them and you pay a small extra fee). This was an amazing and very moving moment that we'll always treasure. I hope they're doing well out there in the big blue! A fantastic place and wonderful conservation project. Highly recommended.
title: A fantastic Turtle hatchery and wonderful conservation project.

body: The Turtle Conservation Centre charges 2000 LKR for a brief walk that lasts under five minutes. Visitors handling one-day-old turtles creates unnecessary stress, not to mention the cramped conditions in small concrete tanks housing hundreds of turtles. It felt more like a commercial operation than true conservation, leaving me disappointed. Overall, it's not worth the visit.
title: Absolutely not worth it !!

body: Initially I also thought that this would be a good project to support but after talking to locals I now see it differently.Apparently, someone is filling their pockets with this questionable business idea. This is NOT an aid project for turtles, with the Rs 2000 will not help a single animal. Only one person fills his pockets.Otherwise, the other turtle stations are all owned by the same operator.
title: Big fraud.

body: Such a nice place! They teach you so much about turtles and they’re so nice and friendly. It’s very clear how much they care about the turtles :) Had the best time ever when releasing baby turtles!!!
title: Very good place!

body: So you think you know about turtles? The folks here showed us an awful lot more. It’s a brief tour. The place operates as a turtle hospital and a safe-house for giving the babies a better start in life. The guide explained the different types of turtle, what they ate, how old they got, when they laid eggs, how long they took to hatch. The newly hatched get medical checks before release! There are also some with missing limbs, and a hope that prosthetic legs can be created. Some turtles can be touched, others will bite your finger off. Read the signs.
title: Learn from the natural world

body: We visited with pleasure these pools housing the different injured turtles, and weirdly in the afternoon we swam four kilometers away with seven turtles surfing the waves., it was amazing to see. The explanations provided by the guide on fin repairs were interesting.
title: Swimming with turtles

body: A superb experience, a very interesting center and make us aware of the human impact on our friends animals, boat, waste, etc. I recommend going to a center like this
title: Visit Turtle Help Centre

body: Horrible. Tiny tiny tanks with enormous turtles in. Am not sure am injured turtle with a missing fin is any better off having been saved and then living out his days in a minuscule cement tank being gawked out. Found it quite upsetting. If this is meant to be one of the few ethical turtle sanctuaries I would not like to see the unethical ones.
title: Sad

body: Nice getaway. I think they're actually doing good things for the turtles. But you know what I do think, there is an albino turtle and I do think they keep it longer on purpose because it's special. Some turtles are missing fins or have swallowed plastic. They don't survive in the wild. Then it's a good thing they're taking them in. There were also baby turtles that we were allowed to hold. Didn't because that didn't feel right. Don't do it! Is pathetic! Furthermore, we got a tour and that was nice. All told, it took about 30/40 minutes. Admission is 2000 rupees pp.
title: Nice.

body: Very friendly and thoughtful staff looking after and doing good for the turtles of Sri Lanka. This place seems very ethical and they know a lot of information. Although the tanks could be slightly bigger for the larger turtles
title: Good experience

body: Educational and entertaining, well worth it especially as it takes just an hour of your time, and for a good cause as well. This is our planet and the turtles here deserve our help
title: Educational and worth it.

body: A wonderful place where injured turtles are actually helped and allowed back into the sea after their recovery. This is a very authentic place. The animals are not pulled from the sea for the purpose of illustration for tourists, but are actually helped here.We could even observe animals that hatched less than 24 hours ago.The entrance fee is fair and is 1500 Rb.We were given a personal tour by a student working there. It was really interesting.If you pass by, make sure to stop and support the project. It is not state-sponsored and is based on a private vehicle and donations.
title: Turtles hospital

body: A great space which emphasises education and reminds us to take care of nature by not polluting and being mindful. This space takes in injured turtles and operates and cares for them, before letting them go back into the sea. Unfortunately there's people who eat turtle eggs, so part of their project includes buying eggs from people who find them, as long as they're maintained well, to encourage people who find eggs to give them to the project rather than eat them. A very important space, definitely recommend going and paying the entrance fee, of 1500LKR per person. It's for a good cause
title: Educational space run by volunteers

body: Located just a short distance from our hotel in Koggala beach this place is a must visit if you are in the area. The entrance fee is very small and each group of visitors is assigned a guide to take you through what the sanctuary does to help the various types of turtles that are found off the coast around Sri Lanka.There are various pools with injured turtles, baby turtles of various sizes and a hatchery. The whole visit takes about 90 minutes and our large party all left enthralled by what they had seen and heard.
title: Hatchery

body: Turtles 🐢 good to see , but in reality we paid for the support of those handicaps poor turtles . We came and there are were many kids from school .
title: Turtles 🐢

body: This is a nice Turtle farm and hatchery. The guide was very knowledgeable and explained the different species of turtles pretty well. These guys are doing really well in terms of restoration of turtles whose limbs have been damaged in the ocean.The beach behind the hatchery is very beautiful. The entry fee of LKR1500 is also very reasonable. A must see option for anyone visiting Galle or Mirissa.
title: Must watch Turtle Hatchery in Galle

body: I went to the Koggala Turtle Hatchery in January 2024 with a group of people from my yoga retreat. At first glance the place seemed very worn down and kinda sketchy, but as soon as we got inside it was clear to me that the people working there had a passion for helping the turtles. There were various bassins with different kinds of turtles and the guide were very helpful in explaining about them all. It seemed kinda scripted or rehearsed, but it was great nevertheless. When I went there they had just gotten a turtle in that same morning, that had been attacked by dogs on the beach - super sad, but also important that they show the harsh truth, however uncomfortable it may be. A curous observation: On the walls in the room with the bassins, they have had previous volunteers write greetings on the walls - it could be fun to know more about how to become a volunteer and what role the colunteer play in the project.
title: Great experience

body: Good place that cares good for sea turtles . You can set a Abbau turtle free on the beach what is a nice experience specially for kids. Very informative staff that answers all questions ! Go there and help them with your visit
title: Baby sea turtles

body: We are so happy to have been here and to have supported the project. Everything was explained to us in excellent English, it is so wonderful what is being done there. Many injured animals whose fins have been torn off by motorboats or fishing nets are cared for there until they can live independently in the wild again. We saw different turtles of all ages, including those that had hatched the day before. We were allowed to carefully touch the little ones. Small breeding station that is run with a lot of commitment. Very interesting for children too. The guide is very happy to receive a tip.
title: Absolutely worth it

body: On initial perspective of this place, it would be easy to see that it is for monetary gain over the benefit of the turtles. This is completely overturned when you understand how committed these people are to protect in the life of turtles throughout Sri lanka. The guide that took us there would not have done, so would he have thought that it was over conservation. There are several concrete tanks, which are replaced with freshwater every day or every two days, and the turtles that are in them are either severely injured and are under care, which can take several years if not decades. These would otherwise have died in the wild. The rescue centre also has eggs in the sand which are collected or brought here by local residence that are at danger of being destroyed by tourism or by consumption. The centre releases hundreds of turtles to the ocean each month in many species which can only be a good thing. All the workers are extremely passionate about the turtles. You have to pay to enter which is only a few pounds and you can also participate in releasing the turtles once they have patched or by watching them hatch and be released.
title: Look beyond the fringes. This place does more good than harm!

body: Visiting this sea turtle conservation centre and hatchery at Koggala, was both insightful, inspiring and tragically sad all at once. 🐢When you learn of the impact humans have on turtles and their environment it breaks your heart 💔. But the work these guys do here to rehabilitate injured turtles and prepare them for release back to the ocean is out of this world - did you even know that prosthetic limbs can be made for turtles?! Our guide's knowledge on each turtle, what their injury was and what was being done to treat them was amazing. He was able to answer any questions and just made this short tour really informative and enjoyable. Definitely recommend
title: Informative & inspiring

body: We rocked up by tuk tuk with a 9 week old baby in a pram, the outside looks a little rough and raw but the man who showed us around, came in early to open for us and was intensely passionate about each turtle, he could tell us all the injuries, medication and treatment being carried out and could explain why each one was either living at the hatchery permanently or would be released. Please support this cause and encourage the younger generation to protect these species.
title: Amazing gem, solely for the benefit of the animals.

body: On the advice of a taxi, a stop to see the turtles was just GREAT to see that there are still passionate people who take care of the nature of the animal species. I loved this moment, thanks to our guide 💖
title: A great educational break

body: This place is amazing. They take such good care of turtles. It is like a special hospital for turtles together with being a farm to hatch new babies and release to the ocean. We went in a group. Some of us were foreign passport holders, so we had to pay foreign dollar rate. But, that collection goes towards looking after the farm and hatchery. I did not mind contributing to such a good cause. We had a guide who explained in English which was very good for us. Make sure you ask for one. It is worth the insight into turtle life and the wide varieties of them and their habitats and live style.Do drop when you are passing by, or yet, make a special effort to go to this hatchery.
title: Amazing Place

body: Great work rescuing injured turtles and then return them to the ocean. Little hatchery too is ensuring many more baby turtles survive. Well worth supporting them.
title: Injured turtles and hatchery for babies helping to preserve turtle numbers

body: Contrary to what we read before our visit. I am pleasantly surprised, the staff takes their time to explain the care provided and it is not an aquarium! This place is a real hospital, a place of retirement for injured turtles!After treatment, they are released at sea.It’s educational for everyone!
title: A sanctuary

body: Small but nice turtle rescue center. The guide explained everything to us in good English and it was very interesting. The turtles are well cared for and treated here. We only did a short tour as a stopover on our journey and were even allowed to hold a small turtle. We can only recommend the visit, the entrance fee is reasonable at 1500LKR per person.
title: Nice and interesting!

body: Very educational, non-profit passionate guide who explained everything and showed the different turtlesThere are a number without 1 flipper, they are waiting for a prosthesis, other animals damaged by fishing hooks and motorboats, those who have eaten plastic are in the worst conditionThe organization pays for premises for turtle eggs so that they can hatch safely in a protected environment and then return to the sea
title: Passionate

body: Was unsure initially as to whether this place was genuine but it really seeks to be doing a great job for the injured turtles it rescues. Fascinating guide and explanation of what was happening with each of the turtles they had and it was clear they were in need of help. Great job they are doing and glad we went to support the cause. Thank you
title: Doing a great job for the turtles

body: Excellent explanation by guide. Carefully explained about the different types of turtles and showed some healthy as well as injured turtles they are trying to nurse back and rehabilitate. A must visit !
title: Must Visit place!

body: Our visit to the conservation was great. Our guide was knowledgeable and you could see how greatly he cares about the cause. He showed us many different stages of turtle development, from eggs to 3 year old turtles. We even got to see how little turtles got hatched and we could hold and touch little and big turtles.I definitely recommend visiting this conservation because by doing so you support its activity and enable the survival of many endangered species of turtles
title: Great experience

body: Expect to be a little shocked at the condition of the turtles here. They are of course cared for and the ultimate aim is for the turtles to be rehabilitated and re-released to the ocean. Unfortunately many are missing limbs and whilst prosthetic limbs are the plan for these turtles they are expensive (approx $2500 I was told) and so it’s a very sad situation whereby you wonder if they will ever get the treatment they need.However I don’t say this to be negative - just the realisation of what we as humans have caused these sentient beings. It was very educational and a positive experience to learn that people do really care- and that they responsibly release baby turtles throughout the year to help their survival rates and ultimately increase their numbers. Definitely worth a visit ! And a donation if you are able to :)
title: Turtle conversation and hatchery Koggala

body: 🇬🇧 The staff at Koggala Sea Turtle farm and hatchery rescues injured or disabled sea turtles to care for them and buy turtle eggs from poachers to save the hatchlings. Visitors to the farm can take part in releasing baby turtles into the sea. Injured turtles find a permanent home at the farm as they are unlikely to survive in the wild depths of the sea. On the plus side, the staff seems to be knowledgeable about turtles and you can learn a lot about this gentle species at the farm.
title: Turtle Farm Koggala

body: The Sea Turtle Conservation Project is a great education experience about all aspects of the sea turtles as well as the threats to their continuing existence. The facility is rather small, but certainly presents a very complete picture of the sea turtles, the various types and has a great number of holding tanks to help injured turtles recover. There is also a small beach section where rescued eggs have been placed for hatching and reintroduction into the wild. Certainly a worth organization and definitely worth a visit (and support).
title: A great educational experience and a great cause!!

body: This isn't a zoo. It's an actual conservation ngo that helps turtles victim of human harm. Most of the patients there lost a leg, an eye or have other injuries sustained from fishing, boat damage or ingesting plastic. All of which have humans to blame. It's a very humble place but the volunteer there will take the time to explain their work in good English. The entry fee is very cheap and they don't get a lot of support so don't be shy to make a donation before you leave. You can only pet a couple of turtles but they love a good scratch on their shells.
title: Educational experience

body: It’s a small sea turtle sanctuary/hatchery where you can see different turtles of various sizes. These turtles are all injured and once the are strong enough, they will be released back to the nature.Our guide was really knowledgeable and shared a lot of interesting facts about the turtles and how the organization operates.It’s not a petting zoo, but a real rescue organization. Absolutely worth a visit
title: Small but fine

body: Very informative with a lot of various turtles and their health on display. They deserve more funding.
title: What wonderful work.

body: Highly recommend a visit to the turtle hatchery: very educational and fantastic work rehabilitating sick and injured turtles with a local vet and releasing them back into the wild as well as a hatchery for eggs. It’s only Rs1000 to visit and you can pay extra to release a hatchling into the sea (must go after 4pm to do this). Fully funded by tourists and donations, inspirational to see how dedicated and involved the staff are. Highly recommend.
title: Highly recommend

body: Informative and uplifting. Saw the visible impact of plastics and the damage we are doing to our environment and fauna. great work done by the team here both in helping turtles to recover and in hatching the next generation in the 'hatchery'
title: well worth a visit and to support this project

body: This is an amazing place if conservation is close to your heart. It is not big and it is not fancy and if you don’t pay attention you will walk past without noticing but we really enjoyed it. It is also a massive wake up call and reminder for what we as humans do to destroy the environment and habitat of some creatures. We had a great guide, and the stories are filled with passion and emotion. It is not great to see all the animals in the state they in, but understanding that they in the best care possible give some comfort. It is not expensive to visit and a great opportunity to donate some extra to a very worthy cause. Well done to the team and people involved in this journey.
title: Very good - Expect a roller coaster of Emotions

body: Oh my if we didn’t need to know what we are doing to the planet this place just tells you! Great guide and a real eye opening experience… absolutely fantastic and learnt so much!
title: Amazing place!

body: I visited Turtle Conservation Project with my university friends as a Field visit. We saw many turtles and some of them are injured. They care about turtles and they gave good care about them. Its a great project and helpful for turtles
title: Great Service

body: Amazing team here! It is obvious that they all really care for the well-being of these magnificent creatures and as an animal lover/defender, it was truly touching to see. The only con about this place is the realization that human behaviors have impacted this beautiful planet and amazing creatures to the point hospitals are needed to save them from what we cause. On the brighter side of things, thank heavens there are places and people who care enough to protect these sentient beings. I opted out but upon entering you are given a detailed explanation from a well spoken team member who is happy to answer any questions as well. Great job guys!!
title: Heros doing great work

body: Do something good and visit the Koggala sea turtle conservation project. I learnd a lot about turtles, we were able to touch them and sometimes its also possible to release baby turtles. Staff there was so friendly and the visit is really worth it.
title: Just Amazing work

body: Great work and amazing guides. The tour was short but thorough. Learnt a lot and got to see many different species. They do great work for the turtles and I highly recommend a visit to learn more about what they do. The enclosures are quite small and the turtles seemed a bit distressed, but most of them only stay for a short time. I hope they have the opportunity to expand and create better facilities for the turtles.
title: Great guides and educational tour!

body: I understand that income is important to up keep the protection of any animals and make sure welfare standards are high but it needs a lot of development. I visited in 2018 and saw very small concrete enclosures with nothing but water in them. From watching some of the turtles, I could see displays of abnormal behaviours which suggests unhappy or stressed. All the turtles could do were swim in circles. Some of the turtles has red eyes which indicate an infection most likely from dirty water.When we visited, we asked how long turtles would stay there and where told up to year to help educate others. I am currently studying animal management and understand that educating about wildlife is important but this should not effect wildlife welfare.Extra experiences of interactions such as handling hatchling should not be allowed as studies have shown that human contact can interfere with their imprinting process. Hand feeding as well gets them used to not foraging for food which may effect finding food once realised as they are used to food from hands.I have reviewed some recent photos and have seen not much in welfare improvement has changed. Many turtles are still swimming in dirty water with no enrichment in their enclosures.I am gratefully that they are saving injured turtles and aims are to protect them but recommend changes need to be made.
title: Needs Improvement

body: Not a real hatchery or conservation. It’s all about imprisoning and catching poor turtles from the beach and selling tickets. They don’t release the turtles. They go hunting for the mother’s on the beach during the season and hold them captive. Don’t give them money
title: Not a conservatory. More like a prison

body: interesting place to know about turtles and the varieties. Learned lot of things about them.recommend

body: They say... the turtles who are injured are kept here for treatments. Thier are couple of big turtles and hatchlings alsi
title: Nice place to visit

title: Interesting little place
