body: It was really nice to visit this sanctuary where they are doing a great work, the elderly man that works there really loves the turtles and was stroking their little heads! You could see the little baby ones and were allowed to hold them which was a nice experience. You could also come in the evening and put the bigger ones into the sea so they could start their new life. Well worth a visit!
title: Lovely Turtles

body: Having watched a turtle lay eggs in front of our hotel it was a pleasure to see the conservation work being undertaken here
title: Great work being undertaken

body: Learned a lot about turtles , the young guide at the place was very informative and enthusiastic about what he's doing. People complaining about 500 rs entry fee is very sad as it's not much when you convert into your own currencies. At least they are trying to rescue some . Kids loved the experience.
title: Good experience

body: They doing sea turtles and eggs conservation. Really good work. They caring and nurturing these little turtles Definitely worth a visit. You can see the newborns and older turtles who are handicapped and unable to be sent back into the Sea, Entrance fee is LKR500/person. Keep up the good work. If you are visiting Koggala side dont forget to visit them. Read less
title: Great experience

body: Good to see turtles being cared for and released when well. Staff helpful and knowledgeable. Easy to access from road or beach
title: Small but worth a look

body: I was surprised at the cost of entry to this place RS1000 and thought, well if it’s going to a good cause. Considering the amount of money they must be taking in the place is very small and large turtles are kept in small concrete baths with no room to swim in. I felt really uneasy about this place. The turtles are practically begging you to rescue them and desperately want freedom. Some have a missing limb and I suspect these poor turtles will never see the sea again and will be held captive in those horrible concrete prisons for the rest of their lives. When I asked about the turtles with missing limbs I was fed some BS that they were waiting on false limbs from abroad! They should rename it ‘welcome to the turtle prison.’I would like a response from this project as to why when making so much money from tourists they haven’t expanded or created a better living environment for the turtles? If I get no response you have your answer... greed, greed, greed.
title: Sea Turtle Conservation Project Koggala

body: This was an excellent place to visit as it is a conservation project and not just a hatchery. Our guide was in a bit of a rush but we took our time to read the material on display and learn a bit about these amazing creatures. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Up Close to the Turtles

body: What a wonderful charity. Damaged and sick turtles were nursed back to health before being released back into the sea. Many were missing limbs from boat damage whilst others had consumed plastic which stops them from maintaining their shells.Got to hold babies too!
title: Amazing experience

body: Nice place and a great guide who told us about the program and the different types of turtles. The guide spoke understandable English. Adult ticket at 1000Rs and children 500Rs. I believe that they are doing a great job saving the turtles and not just a “zoo”Think they had around 15 semi adult turtles at the time we were there, and a tank with a lot of new born from the same morning.
title: Great place. Lovely animal.

body: Nothing fancy here - just very dedicated people doing a great job protecting and conserving the sea turtle population. I would really recommend a visit and please donate if you can to keep their great cause going!
title: Really worth a visit!

body: Knowledgeable guide tells you all you need to know about the rescued turtles. It is only small but doing some worthwhile work in conserving these wonderful creatures. My friend and I chose not to release a baby turtle as we had read that it decreases the turtles overall chances of survival. Please visit and show your support
title: Interesting and informative

body: Great to see this work by volunteers in such a difficult situation. It doesn't take long to visit but you feel like you are helping a great cause 🐢🐢🐢
title: Great conservation work

body: My adult son and I visited this small but worthwhile project, and we were both very impressed by the knowledge of the staff member that spoke to us, and the nature of their work. It was well worth the SLR 1000 each entry fee, and it was sad to learn that many of their rescued and rehabilitated turtles have swallowed plastic bags ( thinking they are jellyfish ) or been injured by boat propellors and nets. The hatchery was also excellent, and we got to say hello to the evening before's new additions of green sea turtles, that hatch in the day but surface overnight. The staff also mentioned that they fundraise for 3D printing of new flippers for injured adult turtles, of course this happens overseas and would be expensive, but at least there is a plan for eventual release when they are fit and strong again. There is criticism of the size of the pens, perhaps with more money this could be expanded but they do the best they can with what they have and you have to commend them for trying. Do visit and give them your support!
title: Very worthwhile project assisting injured and threatened turtles with dedicated staff .

body: Hats off to the team at the Sea Turtle Conservation At Kohala. It is terribly sad to see what we as humans can do such beautiful creatures. Please think next time you want to use a plastic bag. For a sea turtle it looks like jelly fish and a meal but the consequences are just awful
title: Well worth a visit

body: The Tourist Entrance Fee is Rs. 1000 which i truly hope goes to rescuing sea turtle eggs. But it is inHuman to keep wild animals in such small concrete boxes. I would understand keeping small (2 to 3 inch babies) But the adult ones that are more then 2 feet in length it is disgusting. They have no space to swim. They have a couple turtles with missing limbs, which i would say is good they rescued them but they still do not have enough space to swim.Do not waste you money or time visiting these places, unless they change their habits and start working with ONLY the baby turtles.
title: This place is a rip off

body: Turtle conservation is definitely what is needed in these areas due to turtles caught in fishing nets and ingesting plastics. It was interesting to learn about the different turtles and the risks they experience. However, the tanks are quite small and it does look like some want to get out. As they take you to each tank they explain why the turtle is there and what their plan is. All of the ones with an arm/leg missing are meant to get a prosthetic from abroad. They say once this happens they will be released, however I am not sure if this happens or if they keep them there for these tours. We saw some baby turtles which are due to be released once they are stronger. They do a turtle release program as well so I assume you can join them for the releases if it is the right season. I do believe these people are doing some good work, however I am not sure if these disabled turtles are being kept as a display rather than entirely helped.
title: Mixed opinions

body: We came across this place whilst walking along the beach so went in. The first thing we saw was a donation box then we were told we had to pay. Entering from the beach, we had missed the proper entrance from the road. We paid the entry fee which I hope goes towards the rehabilitation of the turtles but I'm not convinced. We were shown around and given explanations of what they were trying to do for the turtles but it was mainly calcification treatments for plastic ingestion which makes the turtles shell soft. The tanks are far too small and as with other reviewers, I too witnessed one of the turtles trying to climb out of it's far too small tank.In theory, they are there to provide aid to injured turtles, in reality, I didn't see much of that going on. Would I recommend - no I wouldn't.
title: Not Impressed

body: Our guide Sam recommended this place and it was worth the SL Rupees 1500 per ticket.This Conservation Project looks after damaged turtles caught in fish nets and hooks, motor boats engines and consumption of plastics. The disabled turtles who have lost limbs and fins, outer and inner shells, part of their jaws, etc are taken care of, operated on, supported and healed.Tgwn released into the sea.The hatchery helps with eggs and release of baby chicks into the ocean daily.The many predators of birds, reptiles, animals, fish, crocodiles , weather , etc will eat /destroy 20%of the eggs straightaway.Of the balance 80%, many chicks may not make it to the oceans due to predators eating the infant chicks.All this is explained in details along with different types of turtles found in Sri Lanka, mating, feeding. Hatching habits.30000 eggs are hatched and released into the water every year, with lives fraught with danger.We got to hold baby chicks, bug turtles and release chicks into the seas. Worth every cent and great experience. Highly recommend.
title: Kind Kohhala Sea Turtle Priject6

body: This place is both wonderfully inspiring and sad. To see the work done here to treat injured turtles is heartening but to see the damage that pollution and nets can do is very alarming. Keep up the good work 👍🏻🐢
title: Inspiring

body: It cost LKR 1000 to enter but it’s worth it and the money goes to a good cause. We were lucky enough to see and hold 1 day old baby turtles that had hatched the night before. Great experience!
title: Nice tour - educational - beautiful turtles and babies!

body: A number of varieties of turtles were in tanks within this sanctuary. Depressing to see these wonderful creatures maimed by carelessness. But here they are safe and feed. It is not like a major tourist aquarium. Aside from careing there is a,so a breeding program. Eggs are batched within their confines. Two days later the little ones are released into the ocean. 1500 rupees if i remember correctly. The place seems genuine.
title: Depressing on one hand...

body: Visited here today and had a very knowledgeable young man give us a guided tour of the project. We were shown turtles that had been rescued with injuries from fishing nets and some that had eaten plastic. We were told about the specific treatment each turtle was receiving and when their estimated release back to the wild would be. Some turtles were waiting for prosthetic limbs, but he said they were struggling to find what they needed, but were hopeful a man in Germany was going to succeed. I hope this happens for them. We observed some newly hatched babies and their release to the wild explained. There was nothing the young man didn’t know about the project. We were able to ask questions and he seemed passionate about their work. I’ve seen some poor reviews about the place. It isn’t a big project, but every little helps. The turtles there would be dead without the care they are giving.
title: Very informative

body: Smaller than other Turtle conservation locations in Sri Lanka. Opens at 8 am (as I remember). There is a guide who explains the Turtle diversity, threats and conservation efforts well. Good place to visit for kids and who ever is interested in conservation of Se Turtles.
title: Sea turtle conservation

body: It was nice to see that turtles have their hospital. There where turtles which need help and this is the place where they get it. Worth visiting. Price is 1000LKR/per person for entrance and the visit lasts 20-25min
title: Nice feeling

body: Visited this Conservation Unit and Hatchery. We were interested to see the treatment for sick turtles before their release ( 2 released that day) as all 6 of us are nurses!Most turtles were recovering from a traumatic amputation of a limb or ingestion of plastic.We were able to handle the baby turtles. There was a selection of the turtles that visit Sri Lanka and the explanation was adequate and interesting if not the most fluent - English being a second or third language.We all found the trip,educational.
title: Educational and interesting

body: Don't read too much into the reviews from those who preach about poor conditions and handling of the turtles. Without tourists these places cannot do as much good. They pay fisherman for eggs which costs them 40c Australian per egg.It was extremely informative and I am sure helped most people to think more about nature and conservation.Sure we handled some day old hatchlings that were to be released that day. Sure the turtles were in a small pond - turtles who were saved by fisherman with flippers removed due to injury.Go and see this place. Make sure you donate.I had checked it out and the place is legit.
title: Great find

body: Very great opourtunity to get infos about the endemic turtles and how to protect them.Price is very low and for a good cause.They had some insured turtles there and lits of newly hatched ones.
title: Great place to get all the information about the endemic turtels

body: The staff work very hard with the project and it was a pleasure to witness their efforts. The newly hatched turtles were so small and cute. well worth a vista keep up the excellent work.
title: wonderful conservation project

body: Like other reviews on here, our driver took us here on the way to our hotel. We paid 500 rupees each to go in and have a tour guide. The tour guide spoke very quickly and was rushed. It was a good experience learning what we could about the turtles as he rushed through and we got to touch a few. I don’t know if that’s a good or bad thing, I haven’t been to a turtle factory before so I can’t judge. The thing that left a sour taste in my mouth is that our guide (who we had paid for!) made it clear that he wanted a tip at the end of the quick tour, standing waiting for us to get our wallets out. It seems that the tipping thing is expected here.
title: Nice but rushed and tour guide wanted a tip!!

body: We visited and learnt about all the different species and plight of these wonderful creatures.We also released a few turtle babies while we were there.
title: Good and informative

body: Thought turtle welfare was their priority but turns out it was making money. The guides handle the turtles far too much!! The size of tanks for the long term injured turtles are too small. So much so they looked didjected and sad. No doubt their mental health has been effected. Rather a short life in the sea then one in a tiny dark tank.I agree with raising hatchlings that are indangered but certainly not encouraging locals to find and disturb the nests.
title: Avoid

body: This is a sad little place which is purely a money-making venture, pretending that they are working to promote turtle conservation. We were talked into going there by our driver, and, I'm sorry to say, naively parted with our 1000 LKR for 2 people. The conditions in which the turtles are kept are cramped and pitiful, there is too much careless handling by staff and tourists, obviously distressing for the animals.Hatching eggs (provided by locals), storing the babies in containers and encouraging tourists to pay to release them disrupts the turtles' natural life cycle and reduces their chance of survival. Nothing at all to do with conservation.There are areas of Sri Lanka where you can swim amongst turtles in the wild. Have a look at these for a much more rewarding experience.
title: Please, please don't go

body: You walk in, pay your 500 rupiah then you go into a room filled with tanks. You don’t know what’s going on and then luckily we had a very competent young man guide us through a mini tour about turtles. He was extremely knowledgeable and I could tell hs really cared. I didn’t know turtles are ticklish .... the turtles could be touched, but only the ones that were herbivores - or baby carnivores. Great information / Good little tour
title: Ninja Turtles

body: The turtles in this are numerous but diminishing. This place is trying to hold back the tide of threatening extinction for these gentle creatures but it must be like trying to hold back the tide itself. While motor boats, pollution and diminishing safe egg laying sights continue to blight these animals it makes you ashamed to be part of the problem as a tourist. It makes me laugh, cynically, that we congratulate ourselves on our environmental and conservation credentials while constituting the main reason these things are necessary. Mad.
title: Great work but fighting a losing battle

body: Like other reviewers we arrived feeling somewhat sceptical and left feeling even more so. Odd that they had one of each type in the 'hospital' and very briefly mentioned that they had released 1,000 babies the previous day...I would have thought that would have been a significant achievement and one that warranted celebration...not a one sentence mention.500r entry is fine. No attempt to explain how funding was spent and guide, as a volunteer expected a tip.Left feeling quite sad.
title: Not convinced....

body: This place is only about money, and not turtles unfortunately :( They say it's turtle "hospital", but I don't believe that. 2 meter-long turtles can't feel good in 4 m^2 pool. Also, the staff working there don't care about visitors using a flash when doing photos. That's very sad :(
title: Sad and cruel place :(

body: We visited with 2 teenager and the guides made it short and interesting. A little place but very caring. They really wants to make a difference and they are using the center to get donations in order to help the spieces.Great experience
title: Amazing place

body: This place was awful, the turtles that are ‘sick’ or injured are kept in tiny concrete baths. They were all clearly extremely distressed, swimming back and forth along the tiny enclosure and trying to climb out. The ‘guides’ regurgitated some facts about turtles but otherwise showed little care or interest in them. They splashed water in their faces when they came up for air to make them snap their teeth. Pulled them out by their shells so people could pose with them for photos. They even had perfectly healthy turtles being held for ‘conservation’ that wouldn’t be released for 3-4 years if at all. ‘Not for profit’ yet they charge 500 rupees per person on entry with no sign that any money is being spent on anything to help the turtles. Please do not go here!
title: Horrible, cruel money-making scam

body: Good for a quick stop off on the way to Weligama beach from Unawatuna, it didn’t cost us any extra with our tuktuk. It’s 500 lkr to get in, worth a quick look. The guide told us lots about turtles and we got to tickle them and hold them
title: Knowledgeable guide explained lots about turtles

body: The place is a dingy conservatory kind of thing with 4-5 turtle ponds.. It will take maximum of 10 minutes to complete your visit with nothing exciting to look forward to! Definetly a non-no for the entry fees charged!!
title: Sheer disappointment.. waste of money

body: Interesting place with 5 species of turtle ... good explanation given about each species, and about the work of the conservation project. Discovered that as we had paid 1500 rupees each (not that we were offered any other price ticket), we were each entitled to release a baby olive ridley turtle into the sea.The project is doing valuable work in rescuing turtles damaged by fishermen etc and also greatly improving the chance of hatching the eggs from the different species. Very happy to support the project.Only slight downside was that the man who gave the talk made it very clear that he had expected a tip, and was quite morose when we didn't give one.
title: Informative and interesting

body: Went for a quick tour, on the way to Unawatuna. They have 5 different varieties of turtles and explained well by the guy. We also got the chance to hold 2days old baby turtle and 20yrs old ones. It’s amazing to see how turtles being protected.
title: Learned about turtles

body: Our driver brought us to the sea turtle reservation. Supposingly it was the first one that was established by private party to save the sea turtles. Even after the destruction of the tsunami, they rebuilt the reservation. Certainly deserves donation to support their good deeds.
title: Meaningful lessons learned

body: When we first walked in we were a bit sceptical but having listened to the whole explanation given by the guide we were glade we went in and gave them our. money. They buy around 30000 eggs from the poachers each year and let them hatch and release them back in to the sea. Furthermore they also rescue injured turtles from fish nets and nurture them before releasing them back. Great cause and we were happy to help!
title: Great place

body: I know there are a lot of mix feelings and reviews about this. I didn't do any research about this farm in Koggala. We were actually having tea at Beach Villa which is 5-10mins walk away, the manager was chatting with us asking what do we plan to do, we told him we plan to have a look at a turtle farm and he brought us to this one. Entrance fee is LKR500/person. It's a small farm with a few tanks. The guy started from the first tank and explain to us what type of turtle it is and allowed us to carry it. I must say I was pretty afraid that I would not be able to handle the turtle's weight and drop it. Thankfully I could, it's sort off a mixed feelings of excitement and anxiousness. He showed us another tank where a baby snapping turtle were swimming forward to chomp his finger. Another tank was a turtle who's flipper got sliced off by a motor boat's propeller and it is unable to dive now. Another tank with a turtle that is blinded by fishing net and the last tank contains baby turtles. The babies are sooo adorable and we get to touch them. Again mixed feelings of excitement, anxiousness and a little yek cause it's of their slippery wet body but you would not care and still want to hold them because they are way to cute. He explained about each type of turtle and the work they do there. At the end of it, he did not ask if we would like to pay to release the turtles or force us to make a donation. Of course the tanks are a little small for some of the bigger turtles but some are hurt and not able to go back to the sea. In a way they are taking care of the turtles (I hope). The tanks look clean and not infected or dirty. All i can wish for is that they are sincerely concern about the welfare of the turtles and will do their part to take care of the sick turtles and to them release it back to the sea when they are fully recovered, and part of the entrance fee collected are used to help the turtles.
title: We enjoyed it!

body: Difficult review to write because it would be easy to dismiss this place simply as a tourist trap, but they are clearly making a difference even if the motives are in the greyest of areas. Clearly this is a money making operation- from the shady spivs on the door taking the entrance fee to the "volunteers" with their hands out for "cash donations" and the gift shop with the old chestnut of an out of order PDQ necessitating cash only!Having said all that it's better that eggs are protected, baby turtles are safely released and injured turtles are cared for even if the motivation and ethics are all skewed towards generating Rupees from sentimental tourists. Whilst whale watching we came across more than a dozen Green Turtles trapped in a drifting fishing net. They had all died a horrible death so even a step in the right direction is a good thing.
title: Mixed Emotions

body: We visited by walking up the beach from our hotel. There is an entrance fee and we saw loggerhead, olive ridley, hawksbill and green turtles in large tanks also some small one day and two day old olive ridley tturtles. They also had eggs of labled turtles in a sand container which were collected in October 2018. Each hatchery allegedly patrols a section of beach to deter animals and people taking laid eggs. We made a donation to release a few two day turtles. Be careful if requested to make a donation it can leave a bit of a hole in your pocket.
title: A needed service

body: Powered by passion, the conservation staff are doing a amazing job. I learned lots and admire the knowledge and enthusiasm of the guides. Keep up the great work.
title: An admirable project ..

body: I'm sure some people would think the turtles are kept for show and not nice. But I found the explanations simple but informative and it was really neat to be able to handle them. I loved it.
title: so cute

body: My husband was hesitant as some conservation places could be dodgy tourist traps (read about the Pinnawala elephant orphanage that treats elephants badly in Sri Lanka), but our driver brought us there as it was on our way, and I did not have time to research. 1000 rupees for 2 which is pricey, for a small run-down place disguised as a conservatory. Small tanks for disabled turtles which looked sad, peasant tourists picking turtles up for photos, guides wanting some tips for little bit of 'guide talk'. I read that you can pay to release a turtle into the wild, and that is one bizzare money-making tactic. Why do we have to pay a conservation hub money for them to release wild animals back into the ocean?! Shouldn't that be what they do in the first place? I am for it if the money goes towards improving their welfare, or conservation efforts, but that pathetic money trap is just downright sad. All in all, a horrible tourist trap existing on the faith and goodwill of tourists, we would not be back nor recommend this place.
title: Horrible tourist trap with little care for turtles

body: Me and my boyfriend arrived early to the sanctuary where we paid 1000 rupees between us, for entrance. When we entered, the small enclosure was a bit of a disappointment. The sanctuary had a few turtles that were unfit for open water, however, their tanks they were kept in was unfair on the turtles themselves (they was trying to climb out). The worker was very knowledgable and told us a lot about the turtles. We was told we couldn't release them until the evening and it was best to buy our tickets in advance to reserve a space in releasing the turtles back into the ocean. We was told it would get very busy at the release time. So we bought ANOTHER ticket each, this time they was 3000 between us (we had spent 4000 in total !!). On arrival in the evening, we entered and there was only 1 other girl in the sanctuary. We wasn't sure, but we got the feeling that she had only paid 500 for the entry fee and still got to release a turtle. However, we try to think positive about the situation and hope the money goes towards helping the preservation of these marine animals. Nevertheless, we released 3 baby turtles :)
title: Loved releasing the turtles but pricey and left feeling scammed.

body: We were shown the turtles and given a talk. Able to hold them. Unfortunately there were no baby turtles to release on our visit.
title: Interesting to hear about the different turtles and the coservation project

body: We visited this place after a recommendation of a tuktuk driver without knowing much about the place. We were told that it was a turtle “hospital” and hatchery. We paid 500 rupees for the entrance ticket. We were appalled as soon as we walked in, two tourists were holding an 8 month old turtle with their bare hands to have a photo with it. We witnessed baby turtles being handled, again with bare hands and no handwashing, which can interfere with the imprinting process. The guides actually seemed to encourage people to touch, poke and pick up the turtles. It felt as though these poor turtles are poked and prodded all day for the sake of tourists entertainment and for a photo opportunity. There were several turtles missing fins after fishing accidents, who were waiting for prosthetic fins (allegedly coming from either the UK/Aus-But the guide showed little knowledge about whether this would actually happen) before they could be released back into the wild; noteably a lovely idea. However these turtles were kept in very small, dark concrete tanks which were not large enough for them to swim around in. The turtles just seemed to be floating around the tank which was horrible to see. The guides were manhandling the turtles by grabbing them by the shell or fin, and lifting them out of the water to show us the injuries, which we immediately said to stop as we could clearly see from the water what was wrong. There were turtles of different breeds kept with no apparent injuries, and when asked, the guides told us that these turtles would be kept for around 4 months however was unable to tell us how long they had been there for.They also told us that when they release the baby turtles, they keep a couple until they are 2 years old because they want to ensure the oceans are populated with older turtles, however they are teaching the turtles to live in captivity, and I don’t see how this is beneficial for the life of a turtle to be swimming in a tiny tank for 2 years. I understand the theory behind collecting turtle eggs and bringing them to a safe place to hatch, and have seen this done very well im countries such as Bali and Fiji, but I was shocked at the practice carried out here today. It was clearly a money making practice with no interest in the animals wellbeing. If you care about turtles and the welfare of animals, please do not visit and support this practice.
title: DO NOT VISIT IF YOU CARE ABOUT TURTLES

body: We were given the option to visit this centre and it was well worth it. They have hatchlings one, two, and three days old. They release them back into the ocean on the evening of day three. You get the hold the two day old cuties and also Monica the10yr old that weighed 15kg. They have a few turtles that have been maimed that they odopted. They have 5 different species. Well worth the visit
title: WELL WORTH THE VISIT

body: Went there with an open mind and left impressed that the Turtles are well looked after and there for a reason. Some of the turtles have injuries that prevent them from survival in the wild and they are actively searching for solutions on how to release them. The staff are also really informative and knowledgeable about the turtles and their breeding and I got the sense that their overall mission was to release them all back into the ocean when they were satisfied they could survive.All in all - well worth a visit. Take water as it gets very hot during the day.
title: Impressed

body: Comprehensive presentation by a well informed volunteer guide. Seperate tanks contained several species of turtle at different ages. Some injured and missing limbs, others due for release soon. 30,000 hatchlings releases in 12 months makes this a positive concern. Well worth a look.
title: Interesting

body: I am torn about this "conservatory". I enjoyed all of the information and I want to believe that the turtles are being cared for appropriately but I cannot tell for sure. My friend and I were the only ones there for a tour and education about the turtles but I wonder, if there were more people how many of them would be handling them constantly. I did however ask how long the turtles are held and our guide informed is that only the turtles who were severely injured and unlikely to survive in the wild were kept where as the babies were released after they reach a certain age. It all seems good in theory but seeing them in small dark little tanks just makes you wonder. Overall it was a nice little place to visit and I hope those babies get released and aren't just held there for tourist profits. I found some tags of people on Instagram with videos of the hatchlings being released, so that gives me hope.
title: Nice Visit But...

body: I can't help thinking that this is just a money making concern. I do not see how being handled all day can be good for the turtles. It also seems a bit convenient that they have just enough holding tanks for injured turtles.
title: I'm really not sure

body: We visited Koggala on a recommendation form our driver without really understanding what it was. It was described as a sanctuary/"hospital" for sick turtles but in our experience it was a grim and upsetting place. The turtles are all in very small, dark,cramped concrete pools. Although some of the turtles there had injuries, many of them did not so it was not clear why they were being kept in that way. What I disliked most was that the guides were constantly encouraging visitors to poke, prod and hold the turtles so that they were constantly being harassed all day by a never ending stream of visitors. I do not think that it is right for wild animals to be treated in this way and I would strongly urge visitors to stay away.
title: IF YOU CARE ABOUT ANIMAL WELFARE DO NOT VISIT

body: perfect people, perfect experience and so cute animals which you can touch. you can see each part of their lives- from small egg on the beach to small cute baby and adult one.nice! you can ´t miss this trip!
title: perfect experience- it takes our hearts!

body: I was concerned about going here after reading some of the reviews regarding the welfare of the turtles. The turtles are in fairly small pools of water with nothing to mimic a natural environment for them, however in moderate defence of the establishment some of the turtles would clearly have died without intervention from places like this. The hatchery appeared to be working with lots of new baby turtles to look at. The guide was honest and knowledgeable and although he asked for a tip was not at all pushy or grumpy if not offered one. I would recommend it if you want to learn a bit about turtles and you can allay any fears of animal welfare by asking the guide questions.
title: Better than expected

body: Really nice place they have nice guide for the explain about the sea turtle and nice experience for my Geuest
title: Tour

body: Entrance fee of 500Rs to be shown around, touch and learn about the turtles. The guide was very knowledgable and told us about the dangers the turtles face and what they do to help the turtles. Some of the turtles are disabled and so it’s kind of like a hospital for them and the turtles are rehabilitated following injury and then hopefully hey can be put back into the wild. Some need prosthetic flippers to be put into the wild otherwise they would not survive. The sanctuary even rang us to help them release some baby turtles into the wild. It’s an incredible experience however they are a not for profit organisation. The tanks are a little small and do not mimic natural environments but the up keep Of the turtles must be a drain on funding. All in all a great experience and we would love to help them our in the future.
title: Great Experience

body: We visited the turtle conservation center today and was it disappointed...our guide was full of passion and knowledge of the turtles!! These volunteers are doing a wonderful job for these beautiful creatures
title: Interesting...well worth a visit

body: Really enjoyed our time there, good tour guide who was very informative. They really care for the turtles. It’s very hands on which I like, got to hold a few of them. We paid extra to release a 1 day old turtle each which was nice. Definitely recommend for sure.
title: Definitely recommend!

body: A very informative visit where we learnt a lot about turtles and saw a wide variety of them. Our guide was very good and answered all our questions.
title: A stop on our way to our hotel

body: We have been here for our Honey Moon during our stay in SriLanka. A group of wise volunteers will guide you through the steps of rescuing and rehab of unlucky and baby turtles.Must go
title: Wonderfull way to learn about these beautifull creatures

body: Interesting place to see the effort being made to hatch turtle eggs and return the young turtles to the sea. Also has examples of different types of larger turtles, some of which have sustained injuries
title: Turtle Hatchery

body: Not very pleasant the chap showing us round must have told us ten times that he was a volunteer so could we pay him. Tell me once fool me tell me twice fool you. Poor turtles though.
title: Turtles

body: On our sojourns to look around, we visited this place as we were intrigued by hearing about white turtle and also the kids were very keen. So the visit was a big learning experience not only for the kids but also for us in terms of knowing more about the different kinds and more about the species. We all just loved the stop by.
title: Quality Time with Turtles

body: This is an interactive tour. You get to touch and pick up baby turtles. There is also a full grown turtle-Monica that we were also able to hold. This is located by a nice unswimmable beach. Thus us a non profit doing good work for the environment.
title: Educational

body: I usually look up any type of animal sanctuary before visiting but this place was recommended by our trusted driver so we thought it would be ok. The guide seemed very knowledgeable about the turtles but then huge red flags went up in my mind after I saw the following:1. Lots of these turtles seemed perfectly healthy, but were still confined to small tanks. When I asked when they would be released, the guide responded either 5+ years or never depending on the turtle. He also said the turtles never change tanks and are kept in the same ones the whole time. This was hugely saddening. 2. They were very pushy for us to hold and touch the turtles. The guide tried to provoke the turtles so they would react in front of us. I told him to stop but he just laughed it off3. One turtle could not stay submerged in the water, apparently due to ingesting plastic. The guide told us he could never be release into the wild. To show us this turtles’ handicap, the guide violently pushed the turtle down into the water and the poor thing popped back up like an empty bottle (3rd picture). I feel like this is no way to treat any animal, handicapped or not. 4. They keep baby turtles on show for the sake of ‘education’. They say this is to show school children the different types of species of turtle. However I struggle to think how these baby turtles can learn survive in the wild (such as imprinting) when they are kept in a tank for most of their youngest years! I felt deeply saddened by this experience. This place definitely put profit before the well-being of the turtles. Please be aware.
title: I regret this visit. Do not go.

body: This place really shocked me. I was expecting to see genuine care shown to sick/injured turtles. However what I saw was quite the opposite. Many healthy large turtles, either isoloated or packed into small dirty concrete pools. It shocked me that I seemed to be the only one who was extremely disturbed by this, also by the way the “guild” encouraged the tourists to hold the clearly stressed turtles roughly under their arms while their flapped helplessly. Many times I asked why the turtle was still in the tanks as they genuinely appeared healthy and fit and they simply replied because “they had eaten too much rubbish” or because one was missing an eye or injured foot, which I completely understand.... HOWEVER, these turtles looked fully recovered and healed! What broke my heart the most was seeing one turtle desperately try get out of the tank- The guild explained how this turtle will never return to the ocean because of its broken flipper and will stay there for over 100 years. To think I paid to see that poor turtle who will never return to the ocean despite its good health will live the rest of its life at this hole. They even had baby turtles swimming in a tank which I couldn’t understand!! Why would baby turtles be in a tank when it’s a turtle realise point??? I asked them this and they admitted it was for show. Pathetic and inhuman. No turtle deserves such quality of life.
title: Tourist trap

body: I really don’t know what I was thinking, going here. I hate animal tourism, but I sort of assumed it was actually doing something for conservation. Maybe it is somehow, but the whole experience made me very uncomfortable. As other reviewers have pointed out, the turtles are kept in small tanks, apparently because some of them have been injured, but I didn’t get the feeling that this project is really about caring for the animals - it seemed to be more about making money. Again, I don’t know what I was thinking but eventually relented and agreed to release a baby turtle into the sea. Apparently I’d paid for this, but hadn’t been offered it when I bought the ticket and really didn’t want to. I don’t know much about turtles but it really didn’t seem to be the best way to go about it. Anyway, please donate your money to a proper conservation cause and spend your time elsewhere whilst in Sri Lanka.
title: Don’t go here

body: Entrance was very basic and once you enter you will see the full scope of the project when you get a ticket its a donation to save turtles. The guides explain in thoroughly and their so friendly and let you ask questions. Its kid-friendly and kids get to touch and hold turtles in person if you visit on the right time you will be able to release newborn turtles to the sea, that's the experience kids and family will not forget.This is a fantastic course and if you visit Koggala please experience and support them.
title: Must see and Experience

body: The buildings and surrounds are very basic, even rustic in places but they are doing their best to save the worlds turtles. There is a small fee if you just want to have the information tour and a look around. It is a tactile tour as you are encouraged to touch the recovering turtles and become familiar with them. As well as looking after injured turtles that have been brought to them, they also recover eggs from nests to protect them from predators, unfortunately including human predators. These eggs are put in protected areas and when they hatch, they are looked after for a day prior to release. For a larger fee, you can have a baby turtle of your own to release. This is usually done late afternoon to avoid the heat of the day. We released 2 turtles and there's a lot to be said for having a small part in helping a baby turtle into the ocean that will hopefully live 130 years and be here long after we are gone.
title: Must do in Koggala, releasing baby turtles

body: This is such a horrible, sad place purporting to be a conservation centre.As soon as you walk in & see these beautiful creatures housed in stark, tiny, concrete tanks you know it's all about the money & nothing else.If that isn't bad enough they then pick up these creatures & pass them around ignorant tourists to have their photos taken. Please do not support this place.
title: Horrible tourist trap

body: Our tour guide really wanted us to see the turtle project as he is actively involved in saving the species. The guide was excellent and very clear in his presentation. The different stages of egg laying and release were explained very thoroughly.
title: Tour Visit.

body: I had reservations about going in here but as most of the tour group were keen my husband and I decided to give it a go.Inside were supposedly injured turtles kept in small, stark, concrete containers, it felt so wrong and sad. To make it worse tourists are then allowed to hold these creatures who were obviously stressed to have this happen.I really feel this place is more about making money than conservancy and if you are an animal lover you really want to give this a miss.
title: Horrible tourist trap

body: Although my wife and I had doubts about visiting a hatching and “educational” turtle farm, we went to this place because one could release a baby turtle...I am still in doubt if we made the right choice. But I also can’t say no to chips, crisps and beer, even though I know they are bad for ones health...After paying 1500rps for the tour, picture, and release ticket, we went inside and saw the small concrete bowls housing lonely turtles.The guide gave us quite good info about the turtles. So that was a plus!The turtles in the concrete bowl missed legs and could not survive in the oceans, and because of that, had been sentenced to become living educational tools...Despite my morale internal fight, which lasted about 1 second, the kids and I went on a photo with several turtles...Then we arrived at the hatchery.We were told that the eggs are bought with the entrance fees and hatched, protected against birds and animals, to make sure that almost 100% reaches the sea. Which sounded like a good thing.My wife has better principles than I have and did not want to hold a single turtle for the picture or release a baby turtle.Sorry kids, if there’s no choice, there’s no fight, so I could take moms baby turtle to the beach!When we walked to beach, the kids and I felt like we were saving these little turtles, because we protected it on its journey to the sea. And after waving them goodbye, we left feeling like we did a good thing.
title: Mixed feelings, but left with the best memory of SRi Lanka

body: I was so lucky to get to the conservation project when no one was there but me. The guide took his time explaining the conservation efforts and outreach to the local community. He also was patient and explained to me the various species, migration patterns, etc. I learned a lot and it was a compliment to a previous experience I had had in Panama, tracking turtles, there, no explanation was offered, but here in Koggala, in this small, but well run conservation center, I learned a lot. The entrance fee is very little and this is really a nice experience!
title: A must stop while in Koggala

body: I'm an animal lover, a real one, not the "I-pose-with-drugged-tigers-in-Thailand-and-eat-fish-at-Seaworld type "animal lover". I like to visit conservation projects and had heard about these types of places since moving to Sri Lanka 3 years ago. The bad points:Tank sizes are far too small and there's no stimulation for the turtle. Essentially its the equivalent or a large tiger in a barren cage in the zoo.They let tourists pick the turtles up (adults and babies) and I asked them about it and they said it was because the tourists wanted to so they couldn't say no. So us as tourists need to stop being selfish selfie holics and think about the turtle welfare first.It's debatable if releasing the babies into the ocean actually helps as they are unable to "imprint" on the beach and therefore dont know where to return to when they need to lay their eggs.The good points:They rescue injured turtles which otherwise would of died (but saying that, maybe better off for some of them instead of those tanks).They educate the public about not eating turtle eggs and buy the eggs back off them. Eating someone's reproductive by products is gross anyway but at least they are saving some.They are informative about the different kinds of turtles and they do seem to be trying to help.All in all, i think they are sitting around 50% ethical and concerned with the turtles welfare and 50% being a tourist trap to just make a buck.Happy to be proved wrong though :)
title: Not as bad as had heard but still not a very good effort

body: We enjoyed a very informative visit to the Project. Our guide was very informed on the history of each turtle and explained in depth why they were there and what exactly had been done to help them. They clearly care about turtles and are trying to do something to help. Yes, the tanks are small for the injured turtles but put into perspective, at least they are caring for them. I am sure the facilities will improve in time. We paid 3000 LKR for a family of 3 and we released two turtles into the sea. The facility is small and the whole visit took an hour. I hope and trust this not-for-profit continues to grow and develop over time.*Not to be confused with the hatchery about 200m away on the same road*
title: Ethical and growing.

body: You can pay a bit more 1500 rupees which is about £7 to release baby turtles into the Indian ocean. Quite emotional and 10 minutes walk from the koggala beach hotel. It's a must do.
title: One of the best things ive done, highly recommended.

body: This sea turtle hatchery is a good place to visit. Thousands of baby turtles are released into the sea as part of their conservation project.
title: Worth to visit

body: Our hired driver took us here, but were not disappointed! The guide had a really nice presentation, you could see that he loves the turtles because he knew so much about them. He gave us several turtles to hold. Our admission ticket included a release of a small turtle into the sea, and that was an amazing feeling! To see how they are running as fast as they can to reach the sea it's pretty nice!
title: Amazing

body: We came here as it was recommended by friends and we weren’t disappointed. It was interesting but sad to see the rescued turtles - yet another reason to ban plastics and take more care with motor boats etc. Much more hopeful is the way local fisherman are selling the eggs they find to the sanctuary to be hatched and returned to the sea. What we hadn’t expected was the emotional response to releasing a new hatchling into the sea. Amazing
title: Spiritual

body: This place just beside the Mirissa to Gale connecting road. Here you can see different types of see turtles which are suffering from plastic poisoning or have lost a limb from fishing net. They are kept in small tubs so you can touch them if you like. But the area is rather small and not properly illuminated. So, if 6-8 tourist comes together the place gets to congested to see anything properly.Best part of the place is that you can release baby turtles into the adjacent sea beach.
title: Good initiative but average presentation

body: If releasing turtles is a prerequisite then call ahead as this only happens on certain days... regardless it's an excellent place to visit... the operation is well explained and it's difficult to imagine better value and as it's self funding donations are welcome
title: Good to see

body: We paid RS1500 each for an explanation/guide, to take photos and to release a newly hatched turtle into the sea. You can pay RS500 just to look though. Without wanting to sound rude, I could hardly understand anything the member of staff explaining things was saying to us. Although, quite early on in his explanation he did ask for a tip which annoyed me when we had just paid RS1000 extra each for him to explain things. We refused so then after that everything was rushed. He didn't take any of the turtles out of the water for us to look at properly like other guides were doing. The main saving grace of this place was releasing a newly hatched turtle into the sea. Unfortunately, even this was rushed though. I was trying to video my partner releasing his turtle first and another member of staff holding the bucket kept pushing it in my face demanding I take my turtle too. I repeatedly told him to wait because I wanted to be filmed releasing mine too. Another good thing is that most of the turtles are injured, so it's nice to actually see somewhere in Asia looking after and rehabilitating animals.
title: Amazing activity but too rushed

body: It's an excellent sea turtle conservatory. We were quite surprised when we entered since the place did not look very big or appealing from outside. They have all types of sea turtles and do a wonderful job in conserving and caring for them. Do visit, at least to play with the turtles for a wonderful photo-op!
title: Must visit if in Koggala!

body: A very small place with around 10-12 pools with various types of turtles. Some are awaiting return to the sea after treatment, others been rescued following injuries. Also have a hatchery and for an extra 1000 rupees you can release one to sea. Guides show you round and pass on their knowledge, tip expected!!
title: Great way to spend 20+ minutes

body: Let me first say I know nothing about turtles.The guide told us a lot of information and seemed quite knowledgeable. The turtles we saw were injured and being cared for which gives you a nice feeling that you are supporting a good cause by paying the entrance ticket. How much of it is true, I don’t know. Are the bassin big enough? Are the turtles fed properly? Are they ever put back in the ocean or do the owner have a few injured turtles for you to get emotional and tip more and feel good about yourself?I also didn’t like that all visitors could pick up a big turtle out of its bassin to hold it, is it really ok ? For us it’s great but the turtle sure didn’t seem to enjoy it.We then released our baby turtles in the ocean which is an amazing experience i will always remember (and for which we paid a premium price 1500 vs 500 just to see). But was it the right condition to do so for the baby turtle´s sake ? I don’t know.You basically get what you want from a tourist perspective, good value for money, and definitely an out of ordinary experience and nice memory but as far as the turtles well-being is concerned I can’t say I am convinced this is not only for the money...
title: Liked the idea, can’t validate the way of working

body: Not for profit operation appeared to be well run and talks were informative. Yes, I have heard negative comments about the size of tanks and release of turtles at times to suit paying customers rather than at night but overall I found no issue. There will always be downsides of any operation and the 500LKR entrance fee was reasonable.Unlike others who had to rush off, we asked to exit to the beach and had a delightful walk into Koggala.
title: Well with a visit (and a walk along the beach)

body: Horrible place! Turtles in small tanks, taken out of the water for photos, going from one tourist's hand to another... It's even possible for a tourist to put a baby turtle in the sea (if you pay 1500 rupies of course). Is it a conservation project???? Don't come here. It is a very sad place.
title: All about the money

body: It might seem expensive for the entrance fee of 1500 rupees but you'll soon realize that you are supporting a very good cause and helping the survival of endangered turtles.Well presented and well explained tour from a professional guide.Different types of turtles seen,some injured to be nursed back to health so they can be released back to the ocean.A couple are not so lucky and will never go back to the ocean.They keep the eggs safe here until they are hatched and the baby turtles are released in the ocean.Very educational and for animals lovers.
title: Learning about turtles

body: Seems great and was educational. The guys do a nice job of giving a presentation and personal experience.
title: Tourist

body: Price for entrance ticket 500 Rp, price for realsing baby turtles to the sea 1500 Rp. We get know later that day, it´s very high risk to release baby turtles to the sea during the day as we did, unfortunatelly we didn´t know it. That´s why they get to be born in the night, so they got better chance to survive. Obviously this hatchery is making it to satisfy turists and to earn more money, no respect for animals.
title: bussiness hatchery not for help turtles

body: A well presented turtle centre. Informative and good value. Various turtles to be seen, with interesting information about their lives, behaviour and environmental challenges
title: A Good Turtle Presentation

body: 500rupies entry fee is fair to learn some facts about sea turtles, take some pictures and support this initiative.
title: worth the price

body: 500 lkr ticket to see a few turtles in small ponds. Not worth the hassle unless you are with kids. Small children might enjoy the trip
title: Not worth the trouble

body: Visited with my family and it was actually a bit of a highlight of the holiday!The tickets cost about £7 each but I think that this is very reasonable for what you get. You’re taken on a tour of the site and a guide explains a bit about the turtles to you. He shows you some of the animals that are recovering there and the eggs that are incubating in the sand. We also held some 1 day old turtles which was amazing! They’re gorgeous little creatures.We then got to release a baby turtle into the sea which was just amazing! It’s only something very small but you feel like you’re doing your bit for the environment and the species.Definitely worth a visit!
title: Highlight of the holiday!

body: I got to hold a baby turtle and big turtle - need I say more!Very good guide who told us a lot about the turtles and how they help them.
title: TURTLES!

body: Had read comments about this being a money-making venture but I have to disagree. They seemed very knowledgeable and passionate about what they are doing. I felt some of the tanks were a little small but the turtles were injured in some way and needed rehabilitation. I guess it's similar to us going into hospital and being confined in a small space until we recover? It was a privilege to see these beautiful creatures up close and in some cases able to touch or hold them. I know what a battle it is for the baby turtles to hatch (if they don't get eaten first) and make a mad dash into the ocean before a predator gets them, to understand why this organisation take the eggs off the beach, let them hatch safely and offer the chance for people to release them into the ocean. Well worth a visit. It cost very little for such an amazing experience.
title: A must visit!

body: If you are in Koggala or Galle, pay this sanctuary a visit. It does not take long for a brief tour and the entrance fee, that helps fund the project, is pretty low. Our tour guide was very knowledgeable and a graduate of Zoology. All of the local turtles were described fully and we enjoyed the opportunity to handle and get up close to these prehistoric creatures. To be honest, despite being a cynic, I was quite moved. I can understand some reviewers’ negative comments about the size of the tanks but a project like this has to start somewhere and I doubt that it is blessed with extensive resources. We need to look after our oceans and its creatures and to me this is a worthy project. We are going back to release some turtles tomorrow. I cant wait!
title: Fascinating and heart-breaking!

body: This conservation project is doing a great service in rescuing and sheltering turtle eggs where they are covered until they hatched and then are returned to the sea. You can see the newborns and older turtles who are handicapped and unable to be sent back into the wild. The albino turtles are beautiful. A very worthwhile place to add to your itinerary.
title: Worth a visit and most educational

body: Found this very sad- turtles kept in tiny concrete tanks clearly too small for them with nothing else in the tanks by way on enrichment. We were told these were all injured turtles, and some clearly were missing eyes and fins, but others had no discernible injury. I support the conservation of turtles, but this is not how these creatures deserve to be kept. I was sceptical at their conservation credentials due to the conditions, lack of obvious injuries in many of the turtles that would justify them being kept there, and because they freely allowed guests to take the turtles from the tanks and handle them. Turtles were snapping from the tanks out of the water - something I’ve never seen them do when diving with them, except when they are feeding. They also had a sand pit ‘hatchery’ which they encourage locals to bring eggs to. Given that i understand when nests have to be moved out of necessity all the eggs are carefully marked and the overall structure carefully recreated, this practice also concerned me. Overall, highly distressing.
title: Honourable idea, sad conditions

body: One gets close and personal with many kinds of sea turtles.I'd never seen turtles so close and was thrilled. You see from baby turtles to a rare white one. We should all support such projects and save animals in need! Good job guys!
title: Very informative and well kept reserve.

body: Our one year old spoke one of her first words here: "turtle". She was very excited. Great project helping injured turtles. Visitors get to observe turtles very closely after a short introductory talk. At the end, kids can release two newly hatched turtles to the sea. Around $10US for entry.
title: Great for kids

body: We had hired a tuk tuk to take us to the stiltfishermen and the turtle santuary, we werent disappointed.It is only a small place and takes around 30-45 mins, but the guys are very informative and you get to see the turtles close up and even hold them if you want.Some of the turtles have been injured by boats and will go back into the sea when recovered, unfortunately there were others who had limbs missing or blind and would have to stay there.There were also baby turtles, we saw some just a few days old.The entrance fee helps towards the upkeep and the vets fees who visits once a week.Interesting to find out that any Sri Lankan caught with a turtle faces a long jail sentence.Keep up the good work guys.
title: Wonderful work guys

body: Stopped here during a rickshaw ride between Galle and Mirissa and that was a great decision. We received a very informative tour about the different turtles and about the conservation project. Here they keep injured turtles (often injured due to accidents with boats), treat them and afterwards set them back free into the sea. Often people steal the eggs from the beach to make money, but this conservation project also has the initiative to buy these eggs from the "bad people" and hatch them, keep the babies safe for a few days and then release them into the sea. Definitely worth a visit and the baby turtles will put a big smile on your face :)
title: Great initiative

body: It is walkable along the beach from Koggala, quite small, but has a lot of information about the turtles.
title: small sea turtle sanctuary

body: An interesting visit to see 5 of the turtle species. Eggs being nurtured, hatched and released to save these rare and beautifully creatures
title: Great Conservation Project.

body: A great place to spend an hour seeing how locals try to help. Most interesting is the number of eggs they take in and wait to hatch.
title: Excellent

body: It is nice to see this initiative: the people from the hatchery work together with locals in order to safe injured turtles and "lost" eggs. It was great to see and hear about all the stories of their turtles.
title: Nice initiative

body: staff quite knowledgable and interesting to talk to, quite a few turtles to see and you can let one of the babies of into the sea, for a fee of course, a pleasant hour passed by
title: free the babies

body: Our tour group stopped here and it was kind of sad to see the turtles in small pools swimming in circles. One turtle was handicapped. Others were there after boat propeller cuts. After they heal they are released back to the sea. I would just recommend stopping for a short visit to make a donation. They really need the help.
title: Helping sea turtles but they lack resources

body: Very well shown off and English speaking explanation helped us to appreciate the facility. A must stop and see place. Entrance fee was reasonable.
title: Very educational

body: Turtle conservation a must, in this world with more place for us humans and less for the animals, projects like this are so important and need our support, worth a visit, good explanation and guided visit !
title: Turtle conservation a must!

body: With great love for endangered species, I must say this was a wonderful experience. We got very good information about turtles, their history throughout time, and the five different turtles living at the island. The guide spoke well English. We paid to release baby turtles to the sea, an enchanting moment.If something should have been better about the experience, I would have wished to see some of the turtles in bigger pools. This is a conservation project, so among the adult turtles there is only ill/disabled ones at the site. Some of these are in a pool to rest and get medicine. I get that these don't need more space than they do. But two of the turtles will never be healed, as one lost his arm and the other an eye. I think these two turtles should have had more interesting surroundings than the small pools they lived in. Otherwise a great thing to do and a great cause to support with a small amount of your holiday money. We stayed there for about an hour and bought the ticket to release turtles to the sea (1500 Sri Lankan rupee).
title: Great experience!!
Well worth an hour of your time
body: Situated 10-15 mins East of Galle on the main A2 coast road. Entrance fee is 500 SR and you can tip your guide if you like. You will be told about the five varieties of turtle that frequent the shores of SL and there are a number to f tanks containing turtles that have been injured. Some if these will rehabilitat and be released but others sadly would not survive in the wild. There are also baby turtles that have hatched and will be released and a place where turtle eggs are buried ready for hatching after a few weeks of incubation.its better than some similar places I have been to before and well worth a visit if you are nearby or passing

title: A worthwhile project to support
body: This was a very informative couple of hours. The volunteers are very enthusiastic and keen and give some good informative briefs. Very lucky to be able to handle some of the turtles.

title: Small and wonderful place!
body: On our way to the south of Sri we noticed this place of turtles. Different sizes of them so sweet and nice. Don't remember how much the entrance is, but still not expensive. Not many people. You are allowed to touch all turtles even small.

title: Lovely, considerate conservation project for Sea Turtles :)
body: Well worth a visit to this very considerate, friendly facility. Buildings a little shabby, but all the staff have very big hearts :) Family of 4 adults. A very well-informed conservation staff member gave us a fully-informed visit. Not only do they run their conservation project, but local fisherman - who find egg batches in the local sands bring them here - where they are carefully re-buried, dated, hatched and released. They also rehabilitate injured Sea Turtles - or care for them if they are too injured to be released. Adult entry Rs500 each, plus the opportunity at Rs1500 each to release baby turtles into the ocean, when ready. However, I had to laugh. Although we paid for all this for our two grown children .... the very next day, we were sunbathing on the nearby beach when there were loud shouts from some local people.... a nest was hatching! We joined in to dig out and release as many of the sea turtles into the sea as we could ... all for free!!!

title: very interesting and good activity
body: They doing sea turtles and eggs conservation.that is good for turtles future.you visit that place you can see how do it.they give explain about turtles it's good.really good work

title: A very special place
body: The trip to Sea Turtle Conservation was one of the hight of our holiday in Sri Lanka. What an amazing job these guys do in caring and nurturing these little turtles Definitely worth a visit.

title: Small but nice
body: I loved this place.beautiful turtles and baby turtles ready to be put in the sea. A few turtles were injured so would never be going back to the sea
